subject: Forensic export carve-outs & incident notification — negotiating DPA language
messages:
From: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@stellarushealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jacob Smith <jacob.smith@stellarushealth.com>, stellarus-legal@stellarushealth.com
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Forensic export carve-outs and 48h notification in DPA (Sched 4)

Tessa —

Thanks again for the sync earlier. We're reviewing the proposed Schedule 4 redlines you sent and have three concrete concerns we need to resolve before we can accept the DPA language:

1) Notification timing: your draft keeps a 72-hour "initial notification" window. For regulated PHI-adjacent datasets we have to work to a 48-hour initial notify clock (ours is driven by our incident playbook). Can Redwood support a 48h initial acknowledgment and still carry forward the staged investigation timeline?

2) Forensic export scope: we need clearer carve-outs so that operational telemetry (aggregated telemetry, anonymized model performance logs) are explicitly excluded from the "export of Customer Data" definition. Our legal/security teams cannot consent to broad exports of aggregated telemetry without an explicit carve-out.

3) Subprocessor involvement and backups: please confirm whether backup/replication subprocessors (including cloud-provider snapshot services and third-party backups) are in scope for evidence exports, and if so, whether Redwood will provide a list of the specific subprocessors used to store backups within 30 days of contract execution.

I've attached our redline highlighting suggested edits (Stellarus_DPA_Sched4_redline_v1.pdf). Jacob is copied for SOC/ops context.

We'd like a short mutual action plan: if you can propose updated language for items 1–3 by EOD tomorrow we'll aim to return a final sign-off within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Anna
Anna Ruiz
Deputy General Counsel
Stellarus Health

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@stellarushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forensic export carve-outs and 48h notification in DPA (Sched 4)

Anna —

Appreciate the redlines and the clear asks. Quick responses inline, and an attached proposed counter-redline for your review: forensics-export-grid.xlsx (summary matrix with operational examples).

1) Notification timing: we can accept an initial 48-hour acknowledgement for the trigger that you describe (suspected exposure of regulated data). Operationally, Redwood's playbook currently distinguishes "initial notification" (customer-facing alert) from "forensic snapshot availability." We propose the contract language: "Initial customer notification within 48 hours of discovery; subsequent provision of forensic export or snapshot availability within a commercially reasonable period not to exceed 7 business days unless otherwise negotiated." This keeps the 48h SLA for alerts while preserving flexibility for forensic collection that may require coordination across subprocessors and jurisdictions.

2) Telemetry carve-out: we agree to an explicit carve-out for aggregated telemetry and model performance metrics. Proposed wording: "Aggregated telemetry and de-identified model performance metrics that cannot reasonably be re-associated to an identified individual are excluded from the definition of Customer Data for purposes of forensic exports." That said, if an investigation demonstrates these metrics contain re-identifiable elements, we will treat them as Customer Data.

3) Subprocessors & backups: short answer — yes, backups and snapshot services used to preserve state for production instances are subprocessors. We can provide a snapshot list of backup-related subprocessors within 30 days of execution, and commit to update the list on an annual cadence or upon material change. For evidence exports, Redwood will first attempt to provide tenant-level exports from primary serving infrastructure; if snapshots/backups are required to satisfy a legal or investigative request, Redwood will document the set of subprocessors involved and the minimal set of artifacts to be exported.

Operational proposals:
- We will encrypt forensic exports at rest with customer-specific keys (KMS) and use ephemeral transfer keys for handover.
- We will provide hashed identifiers (one-way salt per-customer) by default; privileged mappings will only be supplied under a lawful request or with mutual action plan approval.

Ben and Vanessa — flagging for any additional operational constraints (regional transfer, escrow options).

I'll attach the counter-redline to the Draft DPA in Drive and push a DocuSign link if Anna indicates legal is comfortable with the 48h/7-day framing.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Legal Ops (Contracting)
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@stellarushealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 14:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forensic export carve-outs and 48h notification in DPA (Sched 4)

Anna/Tessa —

Technical clarifications from infra/security side:

- Subprocessor definition: any third party that stores or processes Customer Data, including managed snapshot services, long-term backup vaults, and cross-region replication endpoints. Those are in scope for exports if the data necessary to investigate an incident resides there.

- Cross-border note: many of our customers have data in both US and EU regions. If an export requires data from non-US regions we will: (a) identify the jurisdictions involved; (b) propose an export banded-by-jurisdiction; and (c) use per-jurisdiction export controls (AES-256 + KMS keys hosted in that region) to reduce transfer exposure.

- Minimal artifact set: our standard forensic export is: metadata manifest (request IDs, timestamps), tenant object dump (schema-limited), log slice (time-bounded), and KV cache snapshot where relevant. We avoid exporting full model weights or generalized telemetry unless explicitly required. We'll include a template manifest in the shared Drive.

- Timeline feasibility: 72 hours to prepare a manifest and initial encrypted export package is feasible for many cases; 7 business days for full handover is conservative but realistic if subprocessors or legal redaction are required. Since Stellarus is asking for 48h initial notification, we recommend the contract separate the two: "notify in 48h" and "export available within up to 7 business days unless otherwise agreed."

Happy to hop on a short tech-only call if that helps accelerate sign-off.

Ben
Sr. Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@stellarushealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jacob Smith <jacob.smith@stellarushealth.com>, stellarus-legal@stellarushealth.com
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forensic export carve-outs and 48h notification in DPA (Sched 4)

Tessa/Ben —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the export grid. That framing addresses the majority of our concerns. A few small edits we'd like to request in the final DPA redline before sign-off:

• Add explicit language excluding "aggregated telemetry" as proposed, and include an example list (model latency histograms, aggregate token counts, anonymized throttling metrics).
• Replace "commercially reasonable period not to exceed 7 business days" with "not to exceed 5 business days for customer-facing forensic export availability where data is within the US; for cross-jurisdictional cases Redwood will notify customer of extended timelines and provide a provisional manifest within 48 hours." This reduces the handover SLA for US-only incidents.
• Insert a clause requiring Redwood to maintain an up-to-date list of backup/replication subprocessors in a shared secure Drive location and notify affected customers within 30 days of any material change.

On the KMS/keys point: we accept the per-customer KMS approach but request an auditable handover log (S3 signed URL generation + access log) that we can reference in a legal/forensic timeline.

If you can incorporate the three bullet edits in the counter-redline and push it back by EOD today we can aim to finalize and DocuSign tomorrow. We're comfortable moving forward with the amended timing and telemetry carve-out.

I'll circulate a final mutual action plan once the redline is updated. Thanks all for fast turnaround.

Anna
Deputy General Counsel, Stellarus Health
